item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00272","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C25","C03","C10"],"selected_candidate_label":"C25","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C25 is a direct predecessor template for the child letter. Both appoint a Special Assistant to oversee foreign economic policy, assign coordination across executive departments, place the appointee at the head of the Council on Foreign Economic Policy, specify substantially the same council membership and participation rule, authorize staff and temporary task forces, and require working relations with the National Security Council and the National Advisory Council. Much of this machinery appears in closely matching language, adapted chiefly to a successor officeholder and updated agency membership. C03 has some parallel appointment-letter machinery involving coordination, staff, task forces, and interagency relations, while C10 shares the Special Assistant appointment and attendance at the same high-level councils, but neither approaches C25's subject-specific and textual correspondence.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"serve as Special Assistant to the President in the area of foreign economic policy ... assisting and advising me in the orderly development of foreign economic policy and programs.
